decision.summary: Tenant reports a failed LG washing machine supplied with the flat and offers to replace it at own cost as their own removable property. This needs landlord consent, so I asked the landlord, told the tenant nothing is agreed, and put the job on hold to 29 July.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: At intake, routine. Landlord consent on the replacement and ownership is outstanding, plus a photo/model from the tenant.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord approval request (APR-101) to the landlord, and an email reply to the tenant on the existing thread; hold until 2025-07-29.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not a human at the agency yet. The decision belongs to the landlord. Escalate only if the landlord cannot be contacted after the review date, since no landlord contact is on file.

args.decision_needed: The tenant reports the LG washing machine (here at the start of the tenancy) has failed with a power fault and says it can't be repaired. They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost, which would remain their property and be removed when they leave. Do you consent? Or would you prefer to repair/replace it yourself, or have us send a contractor to inspect first?
options: Consent to tenant replacing at own cost, tenant keeps and removes it at end of tenancy (recommended if the machine is confirmed beyond repair)
Send our contractor to inspect/repair first
Landlord arranges own repair or replacement
